subject: Day 2: confirm pediatrician visit; stool transition begins
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 2. Stool color is transitioning from black-tarry meconium toward green-brown by today or tomorrow. Target output: at least two wet diapers and at least one stool by the end of today. Cluster feeding in the evening is normal and not a sign of insufficient supply; if breastfeeding, this is the demand signal driving milk-supply calibration over the first week.

Action items
- Confirm the day 3-5 pediatrician visit is on the calendar. If discharged today, the practice will want to see Avi within 24-48 hours. AAP Bright Futures periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Set up the pediatrician's online portal if not done. Most practices route messaging, after-hours triage, and lab results through it.
- Add Avi to your health insurance plan within 30 days of birth as a qualifying life event. Hard deadline. Healthcare.gov QLE reference: https://www.healthcare.gov/glossary/qualifying-life-event/
- If formula-feeding: aim for 1.5-3 oz every 3-4 hours by today, increasing as he tolerates. CDC on infant formula preparation and storage: https://www.cdc.gov/infant-toddler-nutrition/formula-feeding/index.html
- If breastfeeding: keep the feeding log going. Call the lactation consultant if pain persists beyond 30 seconds after latch or if you see frank blood in nipple cracks. IBCLC directory: https://ilca.org/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Cluster feeding in evenings, fussiness between feeds, faint baby acne or milia.
- [low concern] Single black meconium stool stuck in a diaper after the transition has begun. Move on.
- [monitor] Stool still tar-black on day 3 (signals delayed gut transit; ask the pediatrician at the day 3-5 visit).
- [call within 24h] Yellow tinge spreading to the chest or belly (jaundice descending caudally — bilirubin is climbing). Fewer wet diapers than days-of-life. AAP HealthyChildren on jaundice: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Jaundice.aspx
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusal of all feeds, dusky color around lips, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting with each breath, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunity
During an awake-alert window, hold a high-contrast (black/white/red) pattern about 8-12 inches from Avi's face. Newborn visual cortex preferentially tracks high-contrast edges; this is also the focal distance of the nursing position. Two minutes counts.

Upcoming
- Day 3-5: first-week pediatrician visit (target window).
- Day 5-15: cord stump dries and detaches.
- Day 7-10: weight check; most regain birth weight by day 14.

Further reading
- The Happiest Baby on the Block by Harvey Karp — the 5 S's for soothing: https://www.happiestbaby.com/pages/dr-harvey-karp
- AAP HealthyChildren on jaundice: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Jaundice.aspx
- CDC on infant formula preparation: https://www.cdc.gov/infant-toddler-nutrition/formula-feeding/index.html
- International Lactation Consultant Association: https://ilca.org/
